description: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures (BoM) 1.0/1.1: ArcheTypes, EntryNode/Node rules, HasPart XOR IsPartOf, BulkCount, SameAs, version-paired semanticIds, AASd-014 across metamodel revisions.

items.question: Which values may the ArcheType property of a HierarchicalStructures submodel take?
items.expected_answer: Exactly three: Full, OneDown and OneUp.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: ArcheType of the Submodel, there are three allowed enumeration entries: 1. "Full", 2. "OneDown" and 3. "OneUp".

items.question: May the EntryNode of a Bill-of-Material submodel be a co-managed Entity for a part without its own AAS?
items.expected_answer: No. The EntryNode must be a self-managed Entity reflecting the asset administered by the AAS the submodel belongs to.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: Base entry point for the Entity tree in this Submodel, this must be a Self-managed Entity reflecting the Assets administrated in the AAS this Submodel is part of.

items.question: Can one HierarchicalStructures submodel use both HasPart and IsPartOf relationships?
items.expected_answer: No. Either HasPart or IsPartOf must be used, not both.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: Modeling of logical connections between components and sub-components. Either this or "IsPartOf" must be used, not both.

items.question: We need both a OneDown and a OneUp view of the same machine. Can one submodel instance carry both archetypes?
items.expected_answer: No. An instance must only use one archetype; a second (or third) submodel with the other archetype must be created next to it.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: An instance of this Submodel must only use one archetype. If more than one type shall be modeled a second or third Submodel with the specific archetype must be created next to the existing Submodel.

items.question: For a distributed hierarchy built from several submodels, which archetypes may be mixed?
items.expected_answer: Only Full and OneDown; the OneUp archetype cannot be mixed with the other two.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: The "OneUp" archetype cannot be used in a mixed (only Full and OneDown) form with the other two forms.

items.question: Our motor's BoM Node for a specific serial-numbered sensor (an instance asset) carries BulkCount=1. Is that allowed, and what is BulkCount's valueType?
items.expected_answer: No - BulkCount (0..1, xs:unsignedLong) may only be used when the Node references an asset of kind Type (e.g. a 10x M4x30 type screw), not an instance.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: Additional constraint: With bulk count only a reference to an asset with kind type is allowed, e.g., the M4x30 type asset. [unsignedLong] 0..1

items.question: May a HasPart relationship's second attribute be an ExternalReference to the child asset's globalAssetId?
items.expected_answer: No. HasPart/IsPartOf must contain an EntryNode or Node as first and second and shall only reference EntryNodes or Nodes in the same Submodel; the asset link is the Node Entity's globalAssetId.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: The relationships must contain an EntryNode or Node as first and second attribute. The relationships shall only reference EntryNodes or Nodes in the same Submodel.

items.question: Inside a Node, which relationship may have its second attribute point to an Entity in a different submodel?
items.expected_answer: SameAs - its second attribute may contain an Entity element in a different Submodel (even of another specification); HasPart/IsPartOf stay within the same Submodel.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: The Second attribute may contain an Entity element in a different Submodel, including Submodels of a different specification.

items.question: What submodel semanticId does IDTA 02011 v1.1 use, and what changed against v1.0?
items.expected_answer: https://admin-shell.io/idta/HierarchicalStructures/1/1/Submodel; v1.1 changed only the submodel semanticId (v1.0: .../1/0/Submodel) - the element semanticIds such as EntryNode/1/0 stay at 1/0.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.revision: 1.1 (June 2024, admin-shell-io/submodel-templates mirror, tree sha f3790038b6c9, mirrored 2026-10-06)
citation.section: Annex B, Changes Version 1.0 to Version 1.1, Table 1
citation.file: idta-pdfs:txt/published/Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material/1/1/IDTA 02011-1-1_Submodel_HierarchicalStructuresEnablingBoM.txt

items.question: What submodel semanticId does the IDTA 02011 v1.0 specification give?

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material

items.question: Under AAS metamodel 3.0, may a co-managed Node Entity in a Full BoM carry a globalAssetId? What changed in 3.1?
items.expected_answer: Not under 3.0: AASd-014 requires globalAssetId or specificAssetIds for self-managed entities and says they are not existing otherwise. 3.1 dropped that last sentence, so a co-managed entity may carry them.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (as formalised in aas-core-meta)

items.notes: aas-core-meta-v3_1.py lines 3437-3440 (and v3_2 3676-3679) keep only the self-managed requirement.

items.question: Can an EntryNode have no child Node?
items.expected_answer: No. At least one nested Node shall be created under the EntryNode (Node cardinality 1..*), and HasPart or IsPartOf (per ArcheType) uses that Node as second attribute.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: At least one nested Node shall be created as a SubmodelElement for the EntryNode.

items.question: Two sibling child Nodes under the same parent both want idShort 'Sensor'. Is that acceptable?
items.expected_answer: No. A Node's name can be chosen freely but must be unique in its hierarchical (sub-)level, so the siblings need distinct idShorts.

citation.document: IDTA 02011 Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material
citation.quote: The name of a node can be picked freely but it must be unique in its hierarchical (sub-)level.
